title: Stairmageddon
one_paragraph_synopsis: In "Stairmageddon," elevator maintenance forces the Dunder Mifflin employees to navigate the stairs, leading to Stanley's strong resistance and Dwight's extreme efforts to get him to a sales meeting, including tranquilizing and physically carrying him. Meanwhile, a documentary about the office is released with mixed reviews, Senator Robert publicly comes out as gay, and Pam and Jim begin couples counseling to address their marital issues. Andy pursues a music career and impresses a talent agent, while Pam refuses to move her family to Philadelphia despite Athlead's success.

main_threads.thread: The elevator maintenance causes major disruption, with Stanley refusing to climb stairs and Dwight taking drastic measures to get him to a sales meeting.

evidence.snippet: Stanley (growls): I put 17 damn years into this company, and now they're making me climb Stair Mountain!
Stanley: This is an abomination.
Dwight: Stanley is refusing to go out on a sales call.
Dwight: Stanley, one way or another, you are gonna come with me to make this sale.
Dwight (fires tranquilizer gun at Stanley)
Dwight: He's like a manatee. Ready? Let's go again.

main_threads.thread: Senator Robert publicly comes out as gay, crediting Oscar for helping him realize his identity and revealing his relationship with his Chief of Staff Wesley Silver.

evidence.snippet: Robert (on the computer screen): I would just to start by saying that there have been some rumors about my personal life that I would like to settle once and for all. As my long...
Crowd (surprised chatter):
Robert: Oscar is the one who opened my eyes to who I really am.
Robert: –with this new self-awareness, I was finally able to find love at long last. With my amazing… Chief of Staff Wesley Silver.

main_threads.thread: Pam and Jim start couples counseling to work through their marital issues, with Pam refusing to move their family to Philadelphia despite Athlead's potential success.

evidence.snippet: Pam: I mean, we've having issues. It can't hurt to talk about them, right?
Jim: No, no, no, no, no. Uh, we're just starting couple's counseling.
Pam: I'm sure Athlead will be a huge success. But I don't want him to do it anymore, and I don't want to give him an ultimatum, but I am not moving our family to Philly.
Jim: Well, if Pam says she won't go, then— we're gonna need a lot more than counseling.

main_threads.thread: Andy pursues a music career, impresses talent agent Carla, and is accepted as a client despite some skepticism.

evidence.snippet: Andy: I just got a text from my brother. Scranton Times Tribune.com. There's a review of the documentary!
Nellie: "Andy Bernard, the rudderless trust fund child-slash-middle manager, whose incompetence is emblematic of a declining American economy."
Andy (Australian accent): Well, what can't I do? Right, I can sing, I can dance, I can play the banjo, innit?
Carla: Uh, no. We're—we're gonna take you on as a client.

main_threads.thread: Stanley unknowingly closes a sale during the chaotic efforts to get him to the client meeting, much to Dwight's celebration.

evidence.snippet: Stanley: So I just smiled and complimented her grandkids, and we closed it?
Dwight: You earned yourself a nice, fat commission and you didn't even know it.
